text:
incident-bot: Pager alert A-20260317-92: Elevated 502/5xx for service infer-runner-usw2. Error rate jumped from 0.6% -> 12% at 02:07 UTC. Severity: P1. Paging on-call.

max-oncall: I'm up. Who's got gateway samples and node distribution?

lucas-sre: Pulling logs and node map. Early signal from shard runr-7b6 — three pods show repeated crashes: gpunode-11, gpunode-12, gpunode-13. Model-runner process dying with segfaults.

nina-ml: Segfaults are different from pure OOM. Any coredumps? stacktraces?

lucas-sre: Captured one coredump. Sample log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-17T02:06:58Z model-runner[pid=4321]: thread 7 crashed: SIGSEGV ip=0x7f8a3b2e, backtrace: 0x7f8a3b2e 0x556c4a1d 0x556c4a3f
2026-03-17T02:07:01Z model-runner: evicting kv-cache session=abcd-1234 size=2147483648
2026-03-17T02:07:02Z gateway: upstream returned 502 for request id=xyz
```
Process RSS spikes ~200MB right before the crash but host memory remains nominal.

sara-prod: Customer impact: we see top-20k routes with ~12% errors. CS/Support received 3 escalations (EU/APAC). Looping them in.

max-oncall: Mitigation plan: isolate affected nodes, shift traffic to fallback model variant (smaller quantized), enable aggressive prefix+kv caching. devops, can you drain those nodes and change routing?

devops: Running drain: `shardctl drain --node gpunode-11,gpunode-12,gpunode-13 --reason "model-runner segfaults"` — expected ~45-75s. Switching routing after drain.

devops: Drain finished. Applying routing patch to force fallback: `PATCH /routing/policy {"route":"/v1/generate","fallback_model":"redwood-mini-v1-q4","weight":1.0}`

max-oncall: Observability: backend error rate dropped to ~1.1% within 90s. Gateway latency stable. :thumbsup:

lucas-sre: Uploaded coredump: /artifacts/incidents/1760840820/gpunode-12/core. Running symbolication now; initial symbolicate shows crash in attention_kernel.cpp.

nina-ml: Please include the runner binary build id and kernel selection. We need to know if it's an op regression or a memory corner-case with kv-cache growth.

lucas-sre: Runner build: runner-v2.3.0-rc4 (jemalloc tweak + attention-kernel v3). I'll spin an isolated node with v2.2.5 to try reproduce and compare.

sara-prod: Sent customer update: "Temporarily routed traffic to a fallback model while we investigate runtime crashes. We'll update within 30 minutes." Customers acknowledged.

max-oncall: Action items: 1) keep fallback routing for 1h; 2) reproduce on test cluster with same model + runner-v2.3.0-rc4 under load (lucas-sre); 3) symbolicate and triage coredump (lucas-sre); 4) op/kernel triage (nina-ml); 5) node lifecycle + rollback plan (devops); 6) customer comms (sara-prod).

lucas-sre: Repro attempt plan: use stress harness targeting kv-cache growth and long-context prompts. If crash reproduces, collect perf counters and trace attention kernel inputs.

nina-ml: If attention_kernel v3 is the suspect, we can pin kernel selection to v2 for affected models as a short-term stopgap until a kernel fix lands. We should also add an assertion around kv-cache sizes to avoid null-deref.

devops: After smoke checks, reverting routing at 02:43 UTC but keeping the three nodes cordoned `kubectl cordon` until debug/pm complete.

incident-bot: Suppressing repeated alerts for A-20260317-92 for 1h while team investigates.

max-oncall: Good job. Keep thread updated only; we'll convene a 30m check-in if status changes.

sara-prod: Noting customer impact for postmortem: 3 runner pods crashed, ~12% global error spike, 3 paying customers observed errors >40% for ~6-8 minutes before reroute. Saved broader impact with quick fallback.

lucas-sre: Symbolication: looks like null-deref in attention_kernel.cpp:line 214 when kv-cache bucket expands past expected cap. Adding protective checks and extra logging now. Will post rebuild and repro results.

nina-ml: If fix is straightforward guard, we can release hotfix patch to runner-v2.3.0-rc4 as v2.3.1 with kernel guard. If deeper, plan rollback to v2.2.5 across runr-7b6 and pin kernel selection.

max-oncall: Copy. Assigning follow-ups in incident runbook and creating postmortem doc. Owners: lucas-sre (debug & coredumps), nina-ml (kernel/op fix), devops (node lifecycle & rollback), sara-prod (customer comms).

cs-bot: Support ticket updates: #C-10032 (EU customer), #C-10033 (EU customer), #C-10034 (APAC customer) notified.

lucas-sre: Will post back with coredump analysis and repro status. If anyone needs RW access to the artifact path, ping me.

max-oncall: Thanks team. If the crash count increases or fallback doesn't hold, @here escalate immediately.
